findings.claim: [Python/FastAPI 20] Misalignment between objectives and pass mark. Checks 6-8 (the 409 business rules) claim no catalog objective. The six objective-linked checks (1-5 and 9) are 6/9 = 67%, below the 70% mark. A learner who fully shows both claimed objectives fails, while one rule out of two is enough to pass.
findings.recommendation: Either link checks 6-8 to a taught objective (e.g. serving page 'Return 404 with HTTPException', or a business-rule objective), or merge 6-8 into fewer checks so the objective-linked checks reach at least 70%. Record the decision in the blueprint.

findings.claim: [Python/FastAPI 20] One missed argument fails the item. wrong-02 (default 200 instead of status_code=201) fails checks 1, 2, 7 and 8, scoring 5/9 (fail), because checks 7 and 8 assert == 201 as a precondition for the amount rules. A single omitted decorator argument then hides correct cumulative-amount logic.
findings.recommendation: In checks 7 and 8 (and 2), use response.is_success, or 'status_code in (200, 201)', for the setup refunds. Keep the strict 201 assertion only in check 1. Re-run the variant matrix: wrong-02 should then score 8/9.

findings.claim: [Python/FastAPI 20] Labelling: the learner-facing title is 'Python checkpoint question (intermediate): the refund route'. The required 'Python/FastAPI' label is missing from the title, blueprint id/instructions and lab.json. design.md and lab.json notes still call it 'the approved Docker fallback'.
findings.recommendation: Retitle to 'Final assessment, Python/FastAPI coding question 2 (intermediate, 20 minutes): the refund route'. Make the same change in pack/coding-lab/README.md (byte-identical copy), blueprint instructions and the lab.json notes, and drop the 'Docker fallback' wording from learner-adjacent metadata.

findings.claim: [Python/FastAPI 20] Time-box wording differs from the other three items: '20 minutes of coding' here, but 'including reading The task' in the other three. A 109-line README with two tables takes about 4-5 minutes to read, so learners and proctors would apply different clocks.
findings.recommendation: Use one sentence across all four, e.g. 'Time: 20 minutes from the end of setup, reading included.'

findings.claim: [Python/FastAPI 20] Python version is inconsistent: the README says '3.12 or later', the blueprint says 3.12, Python 10 pins exactly 3.12, and only 3.12 is proven.
findings.recommendation: Use 'Python 3.12' with the same check command in both Python READMEs.

findings.claim: [Python 10] Labelling: the title 'Python checkpoint question (basic)' has no time and uses 'checkpoint'. The Spring items say 'final assessment, coding question N (basic, 10 minutes)', and the blueprint says 'Final-checkpoint'. Learners see four different naming schemes across one sitting.
findings.recommendation: Use 'Final assessment, Python coding question 1 (basic, 10 minutes): accepted and rejected records'. Align the blueprint/lab ids too (python-final-basic-validate rather than python-checkpoint-*).

findings.claim: [Python 10] Troubleshooting tells learners to run 'Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned', a persistent security-setting change on the exam machine. Python 20 uses the safer '-Scope Process'.
findings.recommendation: Use '-Scope Process', or offer '.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q' without activating, as Python 20 does.

findings.claim: [Python 10] The scaffolding gives away the two non-trivial moves (raw.get('txn_id'), and loc[0] is the field name), so what is left is a try/except loop plus sorted(). A ceiling effect is likely and the item will discriminate weakly. Acceptable for a 'basic' 10-minute item. Partial credit is sensible: from the matrix, the KeyError slip, loops-twice and newest-first score 5/7 (pass), and first-error-only and try-around-the-loop score 4/7 (fail).
findings.recommendation: Keep the item as is for 'basic'. Optionally drop the raw.get hint and rely on check 3's failure message.

findings.claim: [all four items] The programme timing is stale and has no slack. Both Spring handoffs model the final day as 60+10+20+10+20 = 120 minutes 'zero slack', but the MCQ report moved the MCQ to 90 minutes (150 in total).
